items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: Your saying that you don't look at, don't use music today reminds me of a story that Eubie Blake tells me.

ctx.x: Your saying that you don't look at, don't use music today reminds me of a story that Eubie Blake tells me. And he said that it was unthinkable at least I'll put it this way. That white people simply didn't think that negroes could read music at all. And so they used to have to get the show tunes and whatever else it was because you see these negro musicians as you know, used to play for these rich white people in their homes. The Jim Europe bands that were sent out.

And he said they would get the music and learn all the scores you see and then they would get before these white people and play. And the white people would stand around and say, aren't they fantastic? And they can't even read. (LAUGHTER).
